title: Link expiration
summary: Allow an optional time-to-live when creating a link. Expired links answer redirects with 410 Gone (distinguishable from unknown codes), and link metadata exposes the expiry instant. Links created before the change, and links created without a TTL, never expire.
functionalRequirements: POST /api/v1/links accepts optional expiresInSeconds (positive integer, at most 10 years)
The expiry instant is stored with the link and returned as expiresAt in link metadata
GET /{code} returns 410 Gone with problem type urn:problem:link-expired once now >= expiresAt
nonFunctionalRequirements: Backward compatible schema change: existing rows and the running release keep working
Expiry must be enforced on cache hits as well as database lookups
No additional database query on the redirect hot path

acceptanceCriteria.description: Creating a link with expiresInSeconds=60 returns expiresAt equal to creation time plus 60 seconds
After expiry, GET /{code} returns 410 with urn:problem:link-expired, even if the link was cached
Links created without expiresInSeconds keep redirecting indefinitely and show no expiresAt
expiresInSeconds of zero, negative, or more than 10 years is rejected with 400

assumptions: Expiry is evaluated against the service clock (UTC)
Expired links are kept (not deleted) so their analytics remain available
Stats and metadata endpoints keep working for expired links
outOfScope: Changing or removing the expiry of an existing link
